key_facts: The team decided to drop the speech recognition feature due to its high cost and potential issues with noise disturbance.
The team agreed to keep the L_C_D_ screen and the advanced chip for the display, despite the cost implications.
The team decided to use a single curved design for the remote control instead of a double curved one.
The team opted for a plastic casing with a special color for the remote control, rather than wood.
The team proposed using an integrated scroll-wheel push-button to replace multiple buttons, which would save three Euros.
The team agreed to keep the power button and the menu button, resulting in a total of five buttons.
The team decided to use a hand dynamo as a power source, which would save one Euro.
The team evaluated the remote control on a seven-point scale and scored it a total of twenty-eight points.
The team concluded that the remote control is better than average, primarily due to the L_C_D_ screen.
The team decided to name the remote control 'The Real Remote' and proposed a logo featuring two R's and a one.
The team agreed to use a digital pen for design and presentation purposes, as it was considered more intuitive and effective than other tools.
The team mentioned that the digital pen was more helpful for evaluating designs and graphical content compared to other tools.
The team decided to use a special color for the remote control's casing and button, with the option to add speckles or dots for a more trendy look.
The team discussed the need for recalibration of the drawing tool, which was eventually done using an icon in the presentation.
The team concluded that the project process improved over time, with better team interaction and collaboration.
The team mentioned that the project manager's leadership style became more assertive, contributing to the improved process.
The team agreed that there was enough room for creativity in the project, especially in the design and explanation phases.
The team decided to finalize the report and presentation, with the project manager responsible for writing the report and the team preparing for the final presentation.
The team mentioned that they would need to check their emails for further instructions on the final presentation and project evaluation.
